chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the words of Ali (peace be upon him) regarding the mortgage security deposit, whether both parties would return the excess. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) was saying that'. I said, 'How would they both be returning (the excess)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the mortgage was more than what was deposited with, then it was damaged, the mortgagee would return the excess to his companion; but if it was not equal, the mortgagor would return whatever was deficient from the right of the mortgagee.' He said, 'And like that was the word of Ali (peace be upon him) regarding animals and other than that.'
ai.seo_question: How is the excess value of a mortgage collateral handled if it is damaged or insufficient according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'rad al-fadl' (returning the excess value) in Islamic mortgage law, attributing this specific legal reasoning to Imam Ali (peace be upon him). It clarifies that if the collateral's value exceeds the debt and is damaged, the borrower returns the surplus, whereas if it is insufficient, the lender absorbs the loss, a ruling extended to animals and other assets. This narration highlights the precision of Ahl al-Bayt jurisprudence in balancing creditor and debtor rights within the framework of rahn.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the words of Ali<sup>asws</sup> regarding the mortgge security deposit, whether both parties would return the excess. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> was saying that’. I said, ‘How would they both be returning (the excess)?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was such that the mortgage was more than what was deposited with, then it (security deposit) was damaged, the mortgagee would return the excess upon his companion; but if it was such that it was not equal, the mortgagor would return whatever was deficient from the right of the mortgagee. And like that was the word of Ali<sup>asws</sup> regarding the animals and other than that’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from abu Hamzah who has said the following: “

I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about al-Rahn (security deposit and mortgage) ‘both sides return the extra’. He (the Imam) said, ‘Ali, Alayhi al- Salam, indeed would say it.’ I then asked, ‘How both sides return?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If what is mortgaged is more than the amount the mortgage has provided and it is destroyed, the mortgagee returns the difference to mortgager; if it is not equal the mortgager returns the difference to the mortgagee.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘This is how Ali, Alayhi al-Salam, would say about animals and other goods.’”
